sources.title: Library of Congress: Country Profile, Iran, May 2008
sources.note: Direct institutional PDF read, especially printed pages 2, 3 and 14. Historical transitions and constitutional structure only; obsolete current statistics and early-history simplifications excluded. Same work as legacy loc.gov/rr/frd/cs/profiles/Iran.pdf.

sources.title: Alireza Sheikholeslami, Encyclopaedia Iranica: Administration, Pahlavi period
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read, published 1983, updated 2018. Sections on Reza Shah and Mohammad Reza Shah, bureaucracy and school expansion. Avoid its University of Tehran opening-year discrepancy.

sources.title: National Security Archive: CIA Confirms Role in 1953 Iran Coup
sources.note: Direct archive introduction and document descriptions read, 19 August 2013. Newly released internal CIA history and British/US records establish involvement; archive also emphasizes disagreement over individual actors and mechanisms.

sources.title: United Nations: UNIIMOG background
sources.note: Original indexed UN operational history read. War from 1980, ceasefire 20 August 1988, observers and withdrawal mandate. Earlier /en/mission/past/ path failed; this is the accessible indexed original.

sources.title: WIPO Lex: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Iran, 1989 version
sources.note: Direct institutional record read. Version year 1989, amendment 28 July 1989, Persian material title قانون اساسی جمهوری اسلامی ایران - بازنگری 1368 خورشیدی. The public sample is only the verified Persian document title, not an uninspected PDF-body quotation. Translation is supported by the parallel English title; transliteration is editorial. Signed Persian PDF failed; no facsimile inspection claimed.

sources.title: WIPO Lex: Constitution, English translation, Article 15
sources.note: Original indexed English PDF Article 15 read; direct unsigned URL redirects to record 7697. Persian official/common language and regional/ethnic language literature provision. Same underlying constitutional work as metadata and Persian title, conservatively grouped in final checks.

sources.title: UN Fact-Finding Mission on Iran: Update, 13 September 2024
sources.note: Original indexed official update, opening paragraphs, checked. Jina Mahsa Amini death 16 September 2022, protests and intensified restrictions. Direct PDF 403; no claim of current comprehensive situation or visual inspection.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Trans-Iranian Railway
sources.note: Direct institutional text read, corroborated by indexed ICOMOS evaluation document 189218. 1927 to 1938, 1,394 km, 43 contractors, 224 tunnels including 11 spirals, national-tax financing. The evaluation repeats the same underlying description; grouped as one work if reused.

sources.title: Bulletin of the WHO: Iranian health houses open the door to primary care, 2008
sources.note: Direct full WHO report read through its PubMed Central republication. Household registers, birth/death chart, vaccinations, sanitation; named Maryam Alaini at Afjeh, Iranian and Afghan-born patients. Caption describes latrine building in 1975. Same underlying work as WHO Bulletin original; all three passages counted together.

sources.title: UNICEF: Young Water Guardians, Birjand
sources.note: Direct story by Behnaz Andisheh Rad, 19 February 2025. Sanderos School, 340 Iranian/Afghan pupils, water-drop caps, songs/art, newly repaired taps/fountains/restrooms, Ahmad and Pooya. Report date is not asserted to be exact visit date.

sources.title: UN Iran: Classrooms and latrines in two provinces
sources.note: Direct UNICEF report 20 July 2023. Ten classrooms across five schools, safe water and gender-separated latrines, high Afghan refugee enrolment. Anticipated access benefits not misrepresented as measured attendance changes.

sources.title: UNICEF: Supporting Children and Families During the 2026 Conflict in Iran
sources.note: Direct report by Mehdi Sayyari, 4 August 2026. Disruption to care, safe water and sanitation; health units, vaccine cold chain, purification and psychosocial assistance. Used as dated humanitarian report, not evidence of who started war, military outcome or current leadership.

sources.title: UNESCO: Yalda/Chella, nomination 01877
sources.note: Original indexed institutional description checked in English and Spanish. 2022 joint Iran/Afghanistan inscription; last autumn night, elders, lamp, water, red fruit, poetry, games, gifts. Direct English page challenged. Spanish /es/RL/yald-chella-01877 is the same work.

sources.title: Salvatore D’Onofrio, UNESCO Courier: Nowruz, The seeds of a new day
sources.note: Direct 21 December 2018 article, updated 2023. Haft sin table, seed preparation and fish/rice meal. Origin speculation, universalizing gender claims and inaccurate botanical identifications excluded.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditional skills of carpet weaving in Fars
sources.note: Original indexed UNESCO description read via alternate slug /en/RL/nowruz-00382, whose title and nomination identifier explicitly identify carpet weaving, not Nowruz. Direct canonical page challenged. 2010 inscription; horizontal loom, plant dyes, women’s design and familial instruction. All URLs for nomination 00382 are the same work.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditional skills of building and sailing Iranian Lenj boats
sources.note: Original indexed institutional 2011 description read (query-string variant USL=00534), corroborated by UNESCO decision document ITH-11-6.COM-CONF.206-8+Corr.+Add.-EN.pdf page 24. Stars, named winds, work songs, apprenticeship and pressure from cheaper fibreglass. Same work across mirrors; threats are explicitly dated to inscription account.

sources.title: International Mathematical Union: 2014 Fields Medal, Maryam Mirzakhani
sources.note: Direct official award citation read. Stanford affiliation, dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces/moduli spaces, methods from geometry/topology/probability. Public explanation avoids technical inventions or attribution of all research to Iran.

sources.title: Stanford Magazine: Virtuoso Professor Saw the Beauty of Math
sources.note: Direct 2017 institutional remembrance read. First female Fields medalist in 2014, childhood literary ambition, Iranian Olympiad gold 1994, perfect score/gold 1995, large-paper drawings and daughter calling them painting.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact missing indexed HB record circa 1920 to open end. Islamic Republic alias applies only after 1979. No association with ancient Iranian empires or earlier Persian dynasties. Eight decoded features in identities.json lie over modern Iran; early north edge changes between coarse snapshots, so neither exact borders nor founding date inferred. No runtime/global edits. Final narrative phase has exclusive 2027 endpoint to contain dated August 2026 evidence, not a predicted end.
